pr_title: Add and delete Home Connect devices on CONNECTED/PAIRED and DEPAIRED events
pr_body:
<!--

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
With this PR, the Home Connect will be able to handle the CONNECTED/PAIRED and DEPAIRED events.

- At CONNECTED event handle, the integration fetchs all the data that has not been sent while the appliance was disconnected, and if it is an appliance that doesn't report data while it is off because it also gets disconnected, it populates the coordinator data to later create the required entities
- PAIRED event handle will populate the coordinator data to later create the required entities
- DEPAIRED event will remove the device and left the integration ready for a possible later pairing.

<sub><sup>(message by IssueLinks)</sup></sub>

Please post your question in English, as asking in German here isn’t ideal. The issue you’re experiencing is likely related to the BSH API rate limits. As noted in the documentation you initially linked, all appliances must be turned on during the setup process to ensure their program lists are loaded correctly. 

Furthermore, restarting Home Assistant too frequently can trigger rate limiting, causing all devices to become unavailable for up to 24 hours. Waiting a day before restarting should resolve the issue.

For additional insight, you can refer to this alternative Home Connect integration’s FAQ, which explicitly addresses the rate limit problem:  
[https://github.com/ekutner/home-connect-hass#troubleshooting-and-faq](https://github.com/ekutner/home-connect-hass#troubleshooting-and-faq)

I have the same issue, that appliances and all entities are missing when the appliance is powered off during a HA restart, despite being turned on during the initial setup. The related entities all show 'This entity is no longer being provided by the home_connect integration. If the entity is no longer in use, delete it in settings.' 
I don't think it is due to rate limiting, as it happens even when HA hasn't been restarted for a few days, and I only have 2 devices.
In the HA log there is an error:
`ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.home_connect.switch] An error occurred: {'description': 'HomeAppliance is offline', 'key': 'SDK.Error.HomeAppliance.Connection.Initialization.Failed'}`
It looks like the integration doesn't recognize the appliance at all when its state is 'offline' when the integration is loaded after an HA restart. The Home Connect Android app shows correctly 'Disconnected' for the appliance in this case.

I can say that it is not related to the api rate limits. 

1. I start my device, the washer is rotating.
2. I look into Homeassistant and there is still the old state from one week before. And the state is also not updating. Even after 4 hours. Because i missed the finish :(
3.  It looks like the devices is only updated when the integration is started and the device is on or already running. Not sure which one. 
4. If i restart the integration the correct states are there and it is also updating.

Hope that helps, Many Thanks!

About the OP issue, I corroborate what @RaHehl said, that some appliances if they are not turned on while they the integration is loaded, the entities will not be loaded as there is no way to obtain the status from that appliances.
Anyway, thanks to the work that we are doing with a new library and with the future work that we will do at the integration, Home Assistant will be able to detect new appliances connected and paired and add it automatically to the entry!
